title: dataframe_paths_input_fingerprint is exported but has no caller; deploy uses its own stat-gated duplicate instead
description: dataframe_paths_input_fingerprint is defined and listed in __all__ (execution.py:84) but is never called anywhere in src/ or tests/ (grep over all .py files finds only its definition and the __all__ entry). The structurally-identical consumer that one would expect to use it, deploy/_scorer.py, instead defines and uses its own private _deploy_artifact_paths_input_fingerprint (_scorer.py:199-209) with byte-for-byte identical key/value validation and the same payload shape — differing only in calling _stat_gated_runtime_path_fingerprint instead of the non-gated _runtime_path_fingerprint. So the public function is dead within the repo and is duplicated by the deploy variant, signalling the intended consumer never adopted it. Either delete the unused export, or unify the two (parameterise stat-gating) so there is a single named-path fingerprint helper.
evidence: grep 'paths_input_fingerprint' over *.py: only execution.py:84 (__all__), execution.py:369 (def), _scorer.py:199 (def of _deploy_artifact_paths_input_fingerprint), _scorer.py:793 (its sole call). No reference to dataframe_paths_input_fingerprint outside its own definition/__all__. The two bodies are identical except _runtime_path_fingerprint(Path(raw_path).resolve()) vs _stat_gated_runtime_path_fingerprint(Path(raw_path)).
est_reduction: ~12 lines (remove unused export) or consolidate two ~10-line helpers into one
behavior_preservation: Removing an unused exported function changes no runtime behaviour; consolidating would preserve the deploy call's stat-gated semantics.
